snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹12–25 lakh for a fitted grooming van with water tank, power and two groomers
snapshot.margin_d2c: 30–45% operating margin per groom, before van loan payments
snapshot.margin_production: Groomer pay and consumables are 35–45% of each booking
snapshot.breakeven: 10–18 months for the van model; faster for home visits
snapshot.distribution_note: Local word of mouth, Google Maps and vet referrals bring most clients

tailwinds: Pet ownership has grown fast in Indian cities, and owners increasingly treat pets as family.
Busy owners pay extra for doorstep services instead of taking an anxious pet to a salon.
Pet parents are loyal once they trust a groomer, which makes repeat bookings likely every 4–6 weeks.
Vets, pet stores and apartment communities are easy referral partners.
headwinds: Skilled groomers are scarce and often leave to start on their own.
Traffic limits a van to a handful of appointments a day in big cities.
Parking, water and wastewater disposal at each stop can be a daily headache.
Anxious or aggressive pets bring injury risk to the pet and the groomer.
angle_2026: Pet services have moved from a luxury to a routine expense for many urban owners, and booking apps have made doorstep grooming normal. That also means more competition, so in 2026 the grooming businesses that last compete on trust: the same groomer every time, gentle handling and clear hygiene standards.
cost_basis: Estimated for a home-visit start with a portable kit, and a fitted van as the scaled option, in a metro, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: Professional course, practice on animals under supervision
Folding table, high-velocity dryer, clippers, blades, scissors, shampoos
Your own scooter, or a second-hand one for home visits
Liability cover, trade licence or Shops and Establishments registration
Google Business profile, booking form, uniforms, logo
Van, water tank, heater, generator or inverter, tub, table, fit-out

unit_economics.example: For a ₹1,500 full groom at home:
rows: ₹450–700 per groom before any van loan
unit_economics.note: A van only pays off once it does 4–6 grooms a day, most days. Until then, home visits with a portable kit earn more per rupee invested.

investor_probes: How many grooms can one van or groomer do per day in real traffic?
What share of clients rebook within six weeks?
How do you keep good groomers from leaving?
What happens when a pet is injured during a groom?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start with home visits using a portable kit, build a list of 100–150 regular clients through vets and apartment groups, and buy a van only when your calendar is full most weeks.
sourcing_edge: Buy shampoos, blades and consumables from pet wholesale suppliers in bulk; professional-grade supplies cost much less per groom than retail packs.
licences: Trade licence or Shops and Establishments registration
Commercial registration and permits for a grooming van
GST registration once you cross the turnover threshold
Liability insurance covering the pets in your care

hard_truths.title: Travel eats your day
hard_truths.text: In a big city, driving between appointments can take as long as the grooms themselves. Group bookings by area and day of the week, or your income stalls at three grooms a day.

hard_truths.title: Groomers leave
hard_truths.text: A trained groomer can start their own service with a few thousand rupees of equipment. Pay well, share bookings fairly, and make sure clients know the business, not just the person.

hard_truths.title: Cancellations
hard_truths.text: Last-minute cancellations leave empty slots you can't fill. Take a small advance on booking and keep a waiting list.

hard_truths.title: The van loan
hard_truths.text: A van EMI of ₹25,000–40,000 a month is fixed whether it's busy or not. Buying a van before demand is proven is the most common way this business fails.

plan_goal: The aim is ₹1 lakh in bookings and a list of repeat clients before you buy a van.

plan.title: Validate and prepare
steps: Complete a grooming course or hire a certified groomer.
Talk to 30 pet owners and 5 vets about what they pay and what worries them.
Price your services against 3 salons and 2 apps nearby.

plan.title: Launch home visits
steps: Buy a portable kit and get liability insurance.
Set up a Google Business profile and a simple booking form.
Do 20 discounted first grooms for friends' and neighbours' pets.

plan.title: Build referrals
steps: Leave cards with 5 vets and 3 pet stores and offer them a referral fee.
Post before-and-after photos (with owners' permission) in apartment groups.
Offer a discount for booking the next groom on the spot.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Count grooms per day, rebooking rate and income per hour including travel.
Decide whether to hire a second groomer or add a van.
Raise prices for difficult breeds and long coats.
